Biology Chapter Three Study Notes: Photosynthesis. Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose. It takes place in the chloroplast, which contains the green pigment chlorophyll embedded in the thylakoid membranes. The light dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid and split water molecules, releasing oxygen and producing ATP and NADPH. The Calvin cycle, also called the light independent reactions, takes place in the stroma and uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide into three carbon sugars using the enzyme rubisco. The overall equation is six carbon dioxide plus six water yields one glucose plus six oxygen. Factors limiting the rate of photosynthesis include light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature. Key exam terms: chlorophyll, thylakoid, stroma, Calvin cycle, rubisco, photolysis.
